::: {.tour-intro}
Follow three newly authored, coded Candle Making notes through the real OASIS CLI and MCP server. The recorded assessment uses a deterministic OpenAI-compatible endpoint bound to loopback: no note leaves the machine, no external provider is called, and paid spend is $0. The displayed scores and token usage are fixture values—not live-model assessments.
:::

::: {.tour-notes}
::: {.tour-note-card}
### Real OASIS surfaces

The recording runs binaries built from a clean tracked OASIS source tree at `db2861fdc79aa3bddeaed949c1282e068e7f4eb9`. It exercises the CLI, MCP server, OpenAI-compatible adapter, parser, cache, and evidence code.
:::

::: {.tour-note-card}
### Deliberately bounded inference

The compatible endpoint is a deterministic fixture on loopback—not OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or another live model. Three full-run requests return authored fixture values; external provider calls and paid spend are zero.
:::

::: {.tour-note-card}
### Estimates are not bills

Before execution, the zero-call plan shows a conservative rough estimate of $0.010096; it is not added to observed capture usage. The sample reports 360 fixture tokens and a $0.00084 usage-derived estimate; the full run reports 1,080 and $0.00252. The capture-wide observed estimate is therefore $0.00336. These values demonstrate usage accounting, not provider charges: paid spend is $0, and the MCP cache run adds $0.
:::
:::

::: {.tour-method}
## CLI and MCP: the same operator contract

The MCP view is an actual wire transcript rendered from the OASIS server’s structured responses, not a simulated agent chat. The server is restricted to the synthetic fixture and output roots. The CLI run warms the content-addressed cache; a fresh MCP auto-grade request for the same content then reports 3/3 cache hits with zero new loopback requests, tokens, or estimated cost.

| Operator intent | CLI surface | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| Validate readable inputs | `oasis --format json data validate candle-data` | `oasis.data.validate` |
| Discover records and hashes | `oasis --format json data scan candle-data --rubric rubric/candle-rubric.yaml --hash --summary-only --output evidence/capture/intake-manifest.json` | `oasis.data.scan` |
| Check rubric structure and scoring logic | `oasis --format json rubric check rubric/candle-rubric.yaml --strict` | `oasis.rubric.check` |
| Build the plan and resolve station mapping | `oasis --format json --trace-id candle-plan auto-grade candle-data --rubric rubric/candle-rubric.yaml --provider openai-compatible --output output/capture-plan --max-files 10 --hash --no-transcript --depth shallow` | `oasis.pipeline.auto_grade` |
| Run one-record sample | `oasis --format json --trace-id candle-sample auto-grade candle-data --rubric rubric/candle-rubric.yaml --provider openai-compatible --output output/capture-sample --max-files 10 --hash --standalone --sample 1 --concurrency 1 --no-cache --no-transcript --depth shallow` | `oasis.pipeline.auto_grade` |
| Run the full fixture | `oasis --format json --trace-id candle-run auto-grade candle-data --rubric rubric/candle-rubric.yaml --provider openai-compatible --output output/capture-run --max-files 10 --hash --standalone --skip-sample --concurrency 1 --no-transcript --depth shallow` | `oasis.pipeline.auto_grade` |
| Summarize a completed run | `oasis --format json summary output/capture-run --depth prompt` | `oasis.summary` |
| Inspect results and verify evidence | `oasis --format json inspect output/capture-run --verify --provenance` | `oasis.inspect` |
| Review the provenance ledger (available; not invoked in the clip) | `oasis ledger --limit 10` | `oasis.ledger` |

Except for the clearly marked ledger row, these are the recorded command forms with their capture-relative operands and options. They assume `candle-data/`, `rubric/candle-rubric.yaml`, and the declared loopback provider/model environment; use a configured supported provider outside this fixture. The recording also enables OASIS audit output as capture instrumentation. In the MCP session, `oasis.data.scan` proves record and hash discovery; the station mapping shown here comes from the CLI scan with `--rubric` and the auto-grade plan, not from an MCP scan field. The loopback helper exists only during capture and is not a service contacted by visitors.

Here, **intake** means local file validation and discovery. It does not claim an Elephant upload or managed-data ingestion. Site visitors download only the static page and opt-in recorded media; they do not start OASIS, contact the loopback fixture, or call a provider.

## Complete recorded transcript

<details id="candle-transcript" class="tour-transcript" open>
<summary>Read the eight-step walkthrough without JavaScript</summary>

<ol>
<li><noscript><span id="inputs" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Inputs:</strong> List the isolated working set: three newly authored text notes named DEMO-001, DEMO-002, and DEMO-003, plus the Candle Making rubric and a fresh output directory. The record IDs are codes, not people.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="data" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Data checks:</strong> Run validation to confirm all three files are readable, then scan with hashing and the rubric to resolve three encounters with Note modality at the Candle Making station. This is local intake, not a managed-service upload.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="rubric" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Rubric:</strong> Run the strict checker. It accepts the three Note criteria and their scoring logic before any assessment request or estimated spend can occur.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="plan" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Plan:</strong> Ask OASIS for a dry-run plan. It resolves three encounters and three expected requests, records the selected fixture model, and shows a conservative rough pre-run estimate of $0.010096. Planning makes zero assessment calls, so this rough estimate is not added to the capture’s post-execution usage accounting.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="sample" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Sample:</strong> Execute one bounded record first. One loopback request returns one result with three item scores, 360 fixture-reported tokens, and a $0.00084 OASIS estimate. The response travels through the normal compatible-provider and parsing path so its score, rationale, and evidence shape can be inspected before the full set runs.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="run" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Full run:</strong> Execute all three coded encounters. The CLI makes three HTTP requests to the deterministic loopback endpoint and records nine authored fixture scores plus 1,080 fixture-reported tokens. The full-run OASIS estimate is $0.00252. Across sample and full run, the capture makes four loopback requests and records a $0.00336 estimate, while external provider calls and actual paid spend remain zero.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="mcp" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>MCP cache run:</strong> Start the real OASIS MCP server and call its typed tools over stdio. A fresh auto-grade request for the same three-record assessment is satisfied by three cache hits, so it adds no new loopback requests to the fixture, fixture-reported tokens, or estimated cost. The transcript identifies MCP messages and never impersonates a named model or chat product.</li>
<li><noscript><span id="evidence" class="tour-transcript-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span></noscript><strong>Evidence:</strong> Use summary and inspection with verification to keep results connected to input identities, the rubric, plan, cache status, and provider metadata. The recorded CLI-run verification passes all 22 of 22 evidence hashes; the ledger command remains available for reviewing provenance records.</li>
</ol>

</details>

The [public capture manifest](assets/candle/manifest.json) records the exact source and binary identities, media hashes, execution counts, privacy review, and zero-external-provider boundary. The notes, rubric wording, scores, rationales, and fixture responses were newly authored for this demonstration and are not learner, student, patient, or customer data.
